# Guard for Android

> A free-software (GPL-3.0) Android app that blocks dangerous sites and ads for every app on the
> phone, on any network, by filtering DNS lookups on the phone itself. It also refuses connections to
> known-bad IP addresses, using public lists the phone downloads straight from their publishers. It
> uses Android's VpnService only as a local tunnel that ends inside the app: no VPN server, no
> account, no analytics. Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, with no Google Play services, built for TalkBack and
> large text. The phone companion of the Cocode Guard home-network box.

Built by Babak Bandpey (Cocode, https://cocode.dk). Status: early; version 0.1.1 is released, with
DNS filtering and address blocking (specs 01 and 02 in docs/lean).

Design rules that explain most of the code:

- **Only DNS and listed bad addresses enter the tunnel.** Its routes are a fake DNS address and the
  ranges on the bad-address lists; traffic to a listed address is refused inside the app, never
  relayed. All other traffic bypasses the app. The lists are downloaded on the phone, data only.
- **Stop means stop, said plainly.** If you stop protection, the screen says so. If protection stops
  without your asking, the app posts a notification saying so when notifications are on; if Android
  ends the whole app abruptly, no notification can be posted.
- **Blind-friendly is a requirement, not a polish step.** Spoken labels, live-region status,
  200% font size, and a unit test that checks the palette's text colors against WCAG AA contrast.
